title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties
abstract: arXiv:2610.26496v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reinforcement learning for language models has moved from preference reward models to verifiable rewards, which sustain much longer optimization. Preference models are prone to reward hacking: the policy raises their score without improving response quality, or even while degrading it. Yet for open-ended tasks, where quality can neither be verified nor fully written down as rubrics, they remain valuable. We introduce Dynalize, which mitigates reward hacking online, during policy training. Periodically and asynchronously, a language model analyzes training rollouts and writes penalties for undesirable behaviors that the reward model appears to reward; a judge applies them to every rollout. In clinical counseling and creative writing, training on the reward model alone raises its score continuously but ultimately leads to a decline in external benchmarks; Dynalize sustains longer training and results in improved downstream performance.

translated_title: 通过演化惩罚缓解偏好奖励模型中的奖励作弊问题
translated_abstract: 语言模型的强化学习已经从偏好奖励模型转向可验证奖励，后者能够支持更长时间的优化。偏好模型容易出现奖励作弊现象：策略在不提升回复质量的情况下提高奖励分数，甚至在降低质量的同时提高分数。然而对于开放式任务——其质量既无法验证，也无法完全写成明确的评分标准——偏好模型仍然具有重要价值。我们提出Dynalize，它在策略训练期间在线缓解奖励作弊问题。一个语言模型周期性地、异步地分析训练采样结果，并为奖励模型似乎会奖励的不良行为编写惩罚项；一个评判器将这些惩罚应用到每一次采样中。在临床咨询和创意写作任务中，仅基于奖励模型进行训练虽然会使其分数持续上升，但最终导致外部基准性能下降；而Dynalize能够支持更长时间的训练，并带来下游性能的提升。
tldr: 提出Dynalize方法，通过让语言模型在训练过程中异步分析采样结果并动态生成针对不良行为的演化惩罚，在线缓解偏好奖励模型的奖励作弊问题，从而支持更持久的训练并提升开放式任务的下游性能。
en_tdlr: Dynalize mitigates reward hacking in preference reward models online by having an LLM periodically and asynchronously analyze training rollouts and write evolving penalties for undesirable behaviors, enabling longer training and improved downstream performance on open-ended tasks.
